properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.83.5): a merge deletes the wrong node because the accepted survivor rule picks by provenance and then by id, and sees nothing of status, priority or connections. The code does exactly what the rule says, and a person cannot pick the survivor
properties.source: RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-14, read-only. Scratch import of reflow2 main 26c401b with the published 0.83.5 binary; heal.rs read at origin/main. Data: merge_survivor_pairs.tsv in the dev_reflow2 session scratchpad.
properties.statement:
OBSERVED on 0.83.5, scratch import of main 26c401b. propose_heal, at both balanced and aggressive, proposes two merges, each disclosing "THE ALPHABET CHOSE THE VICTIM":
- keep ctr:anthony (10 edges, no description) and delete who:ajs (1,353 edges), which is the case in fact:apply-heal-would-have-destroyed-the-wrong-contributor;
- keep req:backend_as_product (medium, accepted) and delete req:graph_is_the_content_bible (critical, proposed), which is the case in fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status.

CANDIDATES, each with its refuting measurement and what came back:
(1) The rule's criterion is blind to status, priority and connections, and the code follows it. Refuter: any criterion where the code departs from the rule. NONE FOUND. heal.rs:922–935 provenance_rank (authored 0, unset 1, planned 2 … healed 6) and :1049–1053 (Equal => a <= b, the id tiebreak) are the rule's text exactly, unset ranking just below authored as BL-47 refined it. Nothing in the rule or the code reads status, priority or degree; :3274 only discloses the tie. STANDS.
(2) Bug: the code ignores the accepted degree tiebreak decision. No degree tiebreak exists anywhere (merge_survivor last changed 2026-07-20). That decision's status flipped proposed→accepted in commit 2361a4d3c (#147) with no change record and no approver edge, and the 09-15 ruling decision:ack:d0098626ac85ac53 reaffirms the id tiebreak "UNCHANGED, DELIBERATELY". Whether the owner accepted it is NOT ESTABLISHED, so (2) is unseparated from (1) only on that question.
(3) Data: provenance is mostly blank, so the id decides. In 11 of 11 same-type pairs the id decided and provenance decided 0. Only 5 of 28 node types declare provenance; Contributor, Decision and TemporalFact do not. A contributor to (1), not a separate cause.
(4) The contradiction detector misfires. No accepted decision governs both ends. REFUTED.
(5) The proposer and apply_heal disagree. Both go through merge_survivor. REFUTED.
(6) The judgement pass misread it. Item 23 missed the degree decision. A gap in that reading, not the cause.
(7) Old binary. Reproduced exactly on 0.83.5. REFUTED.

A PERSON CANNOT PICK: apply_heal with keep and remove swapped answered "operation … is not one HEAL proposes for this graph … Nothing was changed."

COUNTS:
- 15 DUPLICATES edges: 1 asserted, 14 suspected.
- 0 live merge proposals today; the one asserted pair, heal:504141f82230f7af, is acknowledged.
- 11 same-type pairs, the id decides all 11. The survivor is less connected in 3 (5 no, 3 tie) and lower status in 0 (4 no, 3 tie, 4 n/a).

THE CLASS: a destructive merge where the engine both proposes AND decides, and the person can only take or refuse the whole. "A person picks" would have stopped all four known cases: BL-47, the storyflow pair, the contributor merge, and the 09-29 rename. A degree tiebreak fixes the contributor merge but keeps the wrong node in the rename case.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the degree decision was ever accepted by the owner; the storyflow pair's degrees; other member designs were not searched. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
